title: Practical hosted slim-handoff and tool-lease PRD (WIP)
summary: Design notes for a lightweight session handoff protocol and a short-lived "tool lease" abstraction to reduce server-side state and improve client-side SDK ergonomics for long-running streaming sessions and structured tool interactions.
context_and_problem: We see two recurring pain points from customer playbooks and SDK bug reports: (1) long streaming sessions keep backend kernel resources pinned (KV cache, tool handles) when clients briefly disconnect or change network; (2) developers struggle with ergonomics around tool-calls that require server-held mutable state (transactional tool responses, multi-step tool workflows). Existing resumable session proposals assume heavy snapshotting or full transcript replay which is expensive and brittle at scale.
goals:
- Provide a low-friction way for clients to relinquish and reclaim operational context without full model snapshotting.
- Make tool-calls first-class but ephemeral: let clients request a short-lived lease/handle for a tool invocation sequence.
- Keep latency and token-cost overhead minimal for common web/mobile disconnections.
- Surface clear, simple SDK primitives so engineers can reason about partial results, retries, and idempotency.
non_goals:
- Not trying to replace full durable session rehydration for audit-compliant workflows.
- Not building a generic workflow engine (that remains solution engineering territory).
user_stories: Frontend dev: mobile chat app - user backgrounding for <1 minute, app reattaches and continues streaming response without re-running the LLM generation from scratch.
Product analyst: multi-step tool call - calls an external summarization tool then a reranker; wants deterministic replay without keeping the external tool connection open on server when idle.
Solutions engineer: enterprise customer wants predictable cost bounds for long-lived assistant sessions where user may step away for hours but should not incur full GPU reservation during that time.
constraints_assumptions: Clients may reconnect on a different region or IP and must be allowed to reclaim context if TTL not expired.
Tool providers (internal/external) may be stateful; we cannot assume every tool supports multi-step idempotent replay.
Latency SLOs for initial reconnection should remain comparable to cold-start (target <300ms extra overhead for reattach path).
primary_approach: Introduce two coordinated primitives: (A) slim-session manifest: tiny server-side token referencing cached prefixes + ephemeral metadata (KV anchors, tool-lease refs) with short TTL; (B) tool-lease API: server issues a lease id when a client begins a tool-interaction sequence. Lease attaches to a slim-session and encodes idempotency expectations and TTL. SDKs expose high-level 'lease' objects that auto-renew while foregrounded and gracefully expire when backgrounded.
requirements: API: POST /sessions/:id/attach with manifest_ref -> validates TTL and returns restored callables and a hot KV window pointer (not full model state).
API: POST /sessions/:id/tool-lease -> returns lease_id, allowed_ttl_seconds, idempotency_token, list of expected hooks (on_commit, on_abort).
API: PUT /tool-lease/:lease_id/commit and /abort to finalize external tool side-effects.
SDK: JS + Python: Lease object with methods: start(), heartbeat(), commit(), abort(), on('renewal'), on('expired').
Observability: tracking metrics for lease churn, average attach latency, expired vs reclaimed leases, failed lease commits.
Security: lease tokens are short-lived and bound to customer project; cannot be exchanged across tenants.
Backward compatibility: defaulting to existing resumable behavior for clients that ignore new fields.
sdk_ergonomics_notes:
- Expose a single simple object: Session.handleLease({autoRenew: true, ttl: 30}) -> returns Lease. Avoid exposing raw HTTP details.
- When backgrounded, SDK calls lease.heartbeat every 15s; on OS-level backgrounding we switch to a passive 'renew on foreground' semantic to avoid battery/network noise.
- Provide helper wrappers for common patterns: transactionalTool(lease, asyncFn) that handles commit/abort automatically on success/error.
- Document best-practices for idempotent external tools and example code for integrating with webhooks.
- Include migration guide for current resumable APIs: how to switch to slim-sessions and where to expect cost savings.
streaming_behaviour:
- If client detaches without releasing leases, slim-session persists references for short TTL (configurable per-tenant). During TTL we keep only lightweight cached prefix and lease metadata in fast KV.
- On reattach: server validates manifest and, if TTL valid, rebinds existing leases and resumes incremental streaming from last emitted token.
- If leases expired during disconnect, server marks subsequent tool interactions as 'cold' and SDK must reinitiate tool-call sequence (SDK should surface reason codes: EXPIRED, MIGRATED, CANCELLED).
structured_output_and_tool_calling:
- Structured output schema includes a 'lease' stanza: {lease_id, lease_ttl, expected_steps}. This makes it explicit which fragments are recoverable and which require replay.
- Recommend default response envelope for tool results to include idempotency_token and an optional persisted_artifact_id for tools that can store results server-side (helps avoid re-run).
observability_and_slos:
- New dashboards: lease_count_by_status, average_reattach_latency, percent_streams_recovered_without_rerun.
- Alerting: high expired-lease-rate (>5% of reconnects) and lease commit failure spike.
- Cost modeling: estimate memory and KV footprint per active slim-session vs full ephemeral model instance.
success_metrics: Reduce full-generation re-runs after short disconnects by 60% within 90 days of launch.
Average reattach latency overhead <= 300ms for 90th percentile.
SDK adoption: >=10 customers using lease primitives in production within first quarter.
Reduce tail GPU pinned time for interactive sessions by 25% for customers adopting slim-sessions.
rollout_plan: 1) alpha: internal + 2 trusted customers, feature-flagged. Validate attach/expire flows and lease commit paths. 2) beta: open to org accounts, add SDK helpers and migration guide. 3) GA: enable on by-default with tenant opt-out for audit-sensitive customers.
implementation_notes:
- Serving-runtime: add lightweight manifest store (redis-like) with eviction and region-aware replication.
- Routing: attach requests will need to route to manifest home or use manifest proxy; consider redirect token to minimize cross-region state transfer.
- Tools: update tool adapter layer to accept lease tokens and return commit/abort semantics; build simulator for external tool failures for testing.
- Backfill: provide a service job to scan expired leases and call cleanup hooks for external tool adapters.
risks_and_open_issues: Tool semantics: some third-party tools cannot support safe commit/abort; need clear fallbacks and documentation.
Security surface: lease tokens increase transient attack surface if not bound tightly; must enforce project-tenant binding and short TTLs.
Edge cases: cross-region reattach to different kernel may lose micro-optimizations or sequence numbers — need migration heuristics.
SDK complexity: auto-renew heuristics must balance network usage vs. TTL misses; mobile heuristics differ from desktop.
open_questions: Should lease heartbeats be pushed by client only or allow server-side renewal for specific enterprise plans?
What is the right default TTL? 30s, 90s, 5m? Need customer data to choose.
How do we instrument and bill for ephemeral tool leases? per-lease-second, per-commit, or absorbed into token costs?
Do we support lease transfer across accounts for delegated workflows?
next_steps:
- Run quick customer interviews (3 customers) to validate TTL expectations and tool semantics.
- Spike: prototype manifest store + simple JS SDK lease wrapper (1 engineer, 2 weeks).
- Draft migration docs and example patterns for idempotent tool adapters.
- Sync with infra and security on token binding and region routing.
notes_to_self:
- Keep PRD lightweight; follow-up PRD for enterprise durable-sessions if demand emerges.
- Avoid overloading the lease abstraction with features early; iterate with SDK ergonomics feedback.
